summary: Read-only prep for turning x11-dispsw on by default (§N): how to force a display-SW vblank release on hardware and prove it lands nowhere; the client-split inventory; the exact default-on change

prep.summary:
READ-ONLY PREP for OWNER_RULINGS §N (git -C /workspace/kf-master show origin/master:docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md:382-406), lens = forcing a display-SW vblank release. No edits/commits/boxes were made. Branches read: origin/v3-dispsw-exp (86b4fa10) and origin/v3-cand-1 (8a682f1b). Ground truth: ogkm-580.159.04 at /workspace/nvidia-gpu-passthrough/research_clones/ogkm-580.159.04.

Mechanism (how a guest forces a display-SW release): a guest GF100_DISP_SW (0x9072) object's release reaches HOST CPU-RM only as the GSP event SEMAPHORE_SCHEDULE_CALLBACK (0x100b), handled by _kgspRpcSemaphoreScheduleCallback (kernel_gsp.c:1109-1135) → dispswReleaseSemaphoreAndNotifierFill (disp_sw.c:129-179) → semaphoreFillGPUVATimestamp / notifyFillNotifierGPUVATimestamp (method_notification.c:549-643, :289-364). Those writers resolve the target by CliGetDmaMappingInfo keyed on the EXACT (client, hVASpace, gpuVA) GSP supplies, bounds-check offset+size against pMemDesc->Size, and write ONLY through pDmaMappingInfo->KernelVAddr[subdev] — a host kernel CPU mapping. kayfabe never creates that mapping (nvos46_map_flags clears NVOS46_FLAGS_KERNEL_MAPPING_ENABLE unconditionally, kf-host/src/lib.rs:258-268), so KernelVAddr is NULL and host RM writes NOTHING and returns NV_OK. That one bound makes a twinned display-SW object write no memory for the guest, regardless of the address aimed at.

The measured 13-run stack (vast 54044296, GA106, traces/v3_display/dispsw_20261003/README.md) forced NO release at all: the three writer functions were entered 0 times and 0x90720101 was never sent. So §N default-on condition 4 ("a release aimed outside the guest's own memory lands nowhere outside the store and guest RAM") is satisfied only VACUOUSLY and has no positive evidence — which is exactly what this lens must fix with a forcing probe.

Probe design (3 variants) extends the existing serial dispsw lane (scripts/bench/display/dispsw_run.sh) under the host kretprobe kfdsw_probe, using the existing bench-only guest-shim mechanism (hook.sh step 4c / engsw_shim.c): a guest program allocs a 0x9072 object on a 3D channel and registers its release semaphore at a chosen GPU VA via the object's software methods (the guest-controlled address field), varied across (1) its own mapped semaphore page, (2) an in-store VA the channel never mapped, (3) a host-hole VA outside store+guest-RAM. The single invariant that closes condition 4 is map_kva_set==0 on every release in all three variants, corroborated by unchanged host-side canaries outside the guest's store+RAM and an empty host-dmesg delta; variant 1 is the mandatory known-positive proving the probe actually fires a release. This run stays read-only because §N's other open condition — "the client split is built" (§N:397-399; kayfabe still opens ONE host client per VM, audit S1-21/S1-22) — is not yet met, and variant 3's canary is precisely the test of that split.
findings: MECHANISM — the only host-CPU-RM path to a display-SW release is the GSP event, never a direct method. On the NVIDIA/GSP stack the GF100_DISP_SW (0x9072) class has NO CPU-RM software methods: dispswGetSwMethods is the stub dispswGetSwMethods_46f6a7 returning NV_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED (ogkm-580 src/nvidia/generated/g_dispsw_nvoc.h:450-452; vtable binding g_dispsw_nvoc.c:225). CPU-RM's dispswConstruct only records logicalHeadId and sets up vblank callbacks (disp_sw.c:100-104; destruct kheadDeleteVblankCallback :125-126). A release therefore reaches host CPU-RM only when GSP firmware posts NV_VGPU_MSG_EVENT_SEMAPHORE_SCHEDULE_CALLBACK (0x100b, inc/kernel/vgpu/rpc_global_enums.h:263), dispatched by _kgspRpcSemaphoreScheduleCallback (kernel_gsp.c:1109-1135; switch case :1526-1528).

MECHANISM — the callback hands CPU-RM an address, VA-space and flags that are ALL supplied by GSP firmware. _kgspRpcSemaphoreScheduleCallback resolves the RPC's hClient→pClient (serverGetClientUnderLock) and hEvent→pDevice (deviceGetByHandle), then calls dispswReleaseSemaphoreAndNotifierFill(pGpu, GPUVA, hVASpace, ReleaseValue, Flags, completionStatus, pDevice) (kernel_gsp.c:1120-1134). GPUVA/hVASpace/ReleaseValue/Flags come straight from rpc_semaphore_schedule_callback_v17_00 {GPUVA, hVASpace, ReleaseValue, Flags, completionStatus, hClient, hEvent} (generated/g_rpc-structures.h:1672-1681). What GSP puts in those fields is CLOSED FIRMWARE — UNVERIFIED whether hVASpace is the guest channel's own VA space and which Flags/addr a guest method produces.

MECHANISM — dispswReleaseSemaphoreAndNotifierFill branches on Flags and either validates the address or writes it. disp_sw.c:129-179: F_SEMAPHORE_ADDR_VALID (bits 0|1) → CliGetDmaMappingInfo(...gpuVA...) and return NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS if not found (:144-154); F_SEMAPHORE_RELEASE (bit 2) → semaphoreFillGPUVA (:155-165); F_NOTIFIER_FILL (bit 3) → notifyFillNotifierGPUVA (:166-177). Flag bit defs: g_dispsw_nvoc.h:55-59.

THE LOAD-BEARING BOUND — host RM writes a release ONLY through a host kernel CPU mapping, which kayfabe never creates, so a twinned 0x9072 writes no memory at all. semaphoreFillGPUVATimestamp (method_notification.c:549-643) and notifyFillNotifierGPUVATimestamp (:289-364): both (a) look up the DMA mapping via CliGetDmaMappingInfo keyed on (client, device, hMemCtx=hVASpace, gpuVA) and return NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS + log 'Can't find mapping; semaphore not released'/'notifier not written' when absent (:581-591, :312-322); (b) bounds-check offset+size ≤ pMemDesc->Size else NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS (:593-599, :324-330); (c) WRITE only via pDmaMappingInfo->KernelVAddr[subdev] and, when that is NULL, log 'KernelVAddr==NULL; semaphore not released'/'notifier not written' and write NOTHING, returning NV_OK (:624-635, :349-359). KernelVAddr is populated only for a map made with NVOS46_FLAGS_KERNEL_MAPPING_ENABLE (bit 5:5), gated everywhere by bKernelMappingRequired (virtual_mem.c:1247, used at :1442-1453, :1483-1488, :1551-1561; GSP path _virtmemAllocKernelMapping :1024-1130). kayfabe clears that bit on EVERY map at the one choke point nvos46_map_flags (kf-host/src/lib.rs:258-268), pinned by tests the_kernel_mapping_bit_is_cleared_whatever_the_caller_sets (lib.rs:2042-2071) and only_the_one_builder_can_name_the_kernel_mapping_bit (lib.rs:2080+). ⇒ on the kayfabe twin KernelVAddr is NULL for every display-SW map, so a release that reaches the writer writes nothing and returns NV_OK silently. This is the mechanism that bounds the object.

THE SECOND TRIGGER — the out-of-band control 0x90720101. NV9072_CTRL_CMD_NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK = 0x90720101 'an out-of-band version of the NV9072_NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK method', params {NvU32 data; NvBool bHeadDisabled} (ctrl9072.h:57-84). Flags 0x48 = RMCTRL_FLAGS_ROUTE_TO_PHYSICAL (0x40, control.h:233) | RMCTRL_FLAGS_NON_PRIVILEGED (0x08, control.h:208), table entry g_dispsw_nvoc.c:176-190. Because it is ROUTE_TO_PHYSICAL it reaches kayfabe on a GSP host; NOTHING in kf3 serves it, so it meets the unserviced ledger and is refused NOT_SUPPORTED (V3_DISPLAY.md open item (d); crates/kf-rm no twin verb built). ⇒ a probe sending 0x90720101 today tests kayfabe's REFUSAL, not a host release — it cannot be the forcing function for a real release on current kf3.

THE REAL FORCING FUNCTION is the object's software methods on the passthrough channel's pushbuffer, not the 0x90720101 control. kayfabe never parses a passthrough ring (OWNER_RULINGS §Q; memory parsing_not_placement_is_what_is_forbidden), so the object's software methods reach host GSP unmodified, and runs 12-13 prove they execute on the host: a twin numbered one behind the guest produced 26 host Xid 32 on that client's own channel (traces/.../README.md:181-194; dispsw.rs IdPlan doc crates/kf-qemu/src/dispsw.rs:49-82,107-120). The guest controls the release target because the object's SET_SEMAPHORE address methods carry the GPU VA (open-driver equivalent encoding, nouveau gf100.c:62-79 methods 0x0400/0x0404 addr hi/lo, 0x0408 value, 0x040c arm; the GF100_TIMED_SEMAPHORE_SW analogue SET_SEMAPHORE_HI/LO in timed_semaphore.c:396-440). The 0x9072 methods themselves are serviced by GSP firmware — UNVERIFIED (closed) exactly which method/addr yields a SEMAPHORE_SCHEDULE_CALLBACK with F_SEMAPHORE_ADDR_VALID.

MEASURED: the stack issued NOTHING. Across 13 serial box runs (vast 54044296, RTX 3060 GA106, host+guest 580.159.04; traces/v3_display/dispsw_20261003/README.md) dispswReleaseSemaphoreAndNotifierFill / semaphoreFillGPUVATimestamp / notifyFillNotifierGPUVATimestamp were entered 0 times in every run ('release calls 0', runs 1-13), and NV9072_CTRL_CMD_NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK (0x90720101) appeared 0 times in every kf3 log (README:102-103,153). Host Xid 0, guest Xid 0, empty host-dmesg delta, all twins freed. Desktop/vsync-GL/X11-vkcube-FIFO all ran. So §N condition 4 has NO positive evidence — it holds only because nothing was aimed anywhere.

MEASURED, scope of 'nothing asked' — it is an inference bounded to HOST CPU-RM, not a proof the guest issued no release. The probe's positive control _kgspRpcDrainEvents counted 1.68-1.98M entries/run (so the kretprobe is not blind), but inside the drain 0 client lookups and 0 device lookups were seen, and the only drain-side lookup usable as a known-positive (CliGetEventInfo, POST_EVENT's) also counted 0 (README:76-85). So '0 lookups ⇒ no release event died early' rests on the drain count working, not on a seen lookup. The guest DOES method the object (runs 12-13); those methods are serviced by GSP firmware WITHOUT entering CPU-RM's release path (README:69-75, 192-194). ⇒ 'no release reached host CPU-RM' is solid; 'no client asked GSP for a release' is not measured.

THE ADDRESS-CHECK SCOPE IS CONTESTED BETWEEN TWO IN-TREE SOURCES, and the newer one wins. CliGetDmaMappingInfo (mapping_list.c:391-447) matches via virtmemMatchesVASpace = (RES_GET_CLIENT_HANDLE(pVirtualMemory)==hClient) && (pVirtualMemory->hVASpace==hVASpace) (virtual_mem.c:988-997) — i.e. keyed on the EXACT (client, hVASpace) GSP names, not client-wide. V3_DISPLAY.md's box block reads it as 'client-wide ... per VA space only if GSP names the channel's own VA space, which nothing here can verify' (V3_DISPLAY.md 'true security bound' §1). The newer memory note security_audit_20261003_privileged_twins.md corrects that: 'CliGetDmaMappingInfo matches the channel's own hVASpace exactly (mapping_list.c:426-438), never client-wide' — so the 'client-wide' phrasing OVERSTATED the exposure. UNVERIFIED either way: hVASpace is GSP-filled (closed). The write bound (KernelVAddr NULL) holds regardless of the scope, which is why it, not the address check, is the one to lean on.

PROBE HARNESS — reuse the existing serial dispsw lane and host witness; do NOT invent a new one. scripts/bench/display/dispsw_run.sh writes /root/dsw/<tag>.log with START/REV/DISPLAY_*/LANE_RC/DSW_TRACE_*/EXIT (wait for EXIT, never 'file stopped growing'); it loads the host kretprobe module kfdsw_probe around the boot via dispsw_trace.sh. The host kretprobe is the only ground-truth witness of where a release lands (a guest cannot see a cross-VA write); its counters are dsw_calls, map_found, map_null, map_kva_set, map_kva_null, dsw_err and per-event va/vas/flags lines (scripts/bench/display/kfdsw_probe/kfdsw_probe.c:43-190,288-304). The guest forcing side reuses the bench-only shim mechanism (hook.sh step 4c, DISPLAY_X11_ENGSW; engsw_shim.c LD_PRELOAD, built in the guest, .so never leaves it) — the release probe extends it from merely allocating objects to registering a 0x9072 object's release semaphore at a chosen VA. Strictly one QEMU at a time; a fresh boot per run (WPR2 resets only on full QEMU restart).

PROBE VARIANT 1 — release aimed at the guest's OWN mapped semaphore memory (the MANDATORY known-positive). Target: a GPU VA the channel has DMA-mapped (the page the X stack's object uses). Host RM per source: GSP posts the callback; CPU-RM resolves client+device (kernel_gsp.c:1120-1126); CliGetDmaMappingInfo FINDS the mapping (the twin did MAP_MEMORY_DMA that VA) → offset in bounds → KernelVAddr NULL (kayfabe never set KERNEL_MAPPING) → 'KernelVAddr==NULL; semaphore not released', write skipped, NV_OK (method_notification.c:624-635). kayfabe sees/logs: kfdsw_probe records dsw_calls>0, map_found>0, map_kva_null>0, map_kva_set=0; kf3 logs the twin alloc + classID readback equal, no GSP REFUSED. Pass criterion: dsw_calls>0 with map_kva_null==dsw_calls and map_kva_set==0 — proves the probe actually FIRED a release (without this, zero release calls means 'none asked', not 'the probe fired and nothing was written'; the exact trap kfdsw_probe.c:22-31 was built to avoid) and that even the legitimate own-memory case writes through no CPU mapping.

PROBE VARIANT 2 — release aimed INSIDE the guest's store but NOT mapped by that channel's VA space. Target: a GPGA/VA resolving to guest VRAM the channel never DMA-mapped (another store slice, or an unmapped offset in its own space). Host RM per source: CliGetDmaMappingInfo keyed on (client, hVASpace, gpuVA) finds no mapping at that VA in that space → NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS, 'Can't find mapping; semaphore not released' (method_notification.c:587-591; disp_sw.c:152-153) → no write. ⊘ Caveat: if kayfabe's one host client has that VA mapped in ANOTHER VA space and GSP named a client-wide context, virtmemMatchesVASpace still requires the hVASpace handle to match (virtual_mem.c:996), so a true cross-space hit needs GSP to name the other space — UNVERIFIED (closed); and even a found mapping has KernelVAddr NULL → still no write. kayfabe sees/logs: kfdsw_probe map_null>0 (no DMA mapping at that VA) or map_found>0 & map_kva_null>0; kf3 log unchanged. Pass criterion: a host-side canary pre-written into that store region is byte-UNCHANGED after the run AND the probe shows map_kva_set=0 (either map_null>0 or dsw_err>0 from INVALID_ADDRESS). Nothing in the store outside the channel's own mappings was written.

PROBE VARIANT 3 — release aimed OUTSIDE the store AND outside guest RAM (a host-hole VA in the twin space); this is the variant that directly answers §N condition 4. Target: a GPU VA that is neither guest VRAM nor guest RAM (a hole in the twin's VA space). Host RM per source: CliGetDmaMappingInfo finds no mapping in (client, hVASpace) → NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS, no write (method_notification.c:587-591); and even were a mapping found, the offset+size bound (:593-599) AND the NULL KernelVAddr (:624-635) each independently block any CPU write — host RM writes NOWHERE. kayfabe sees/logs: kfdsw_probe map_null>0 and/or dsw_err>0, map_kva_set=0; kf3 cannot itself see the release (it is GSP↔host-RM, witnessed only by the host kretprobe); host dmesg delta must stay empty (no NVRM Xid from a bad write). Pass criterion: (i) probe shows the release entered host RM (dsw_calls>0) yet wrote nothing (map_kva_set=0 with map_null>0 or dsw_err>0); (ii) a pre-seeded canary over every host region OUTSIDE the guest's store and guest RAM — specifically kayfabe's OWN host-client allocations (broker frame slots etc.) and, if feasible, a host-RAM page — is byte-unchanged; (iii) empty host-dmesg delta. ⇒ a forced release aimed outside the guest's own memory lands nowhere outside store+guest-RAM (in fact nowhere at all).

OVERALL PASS CRITERION for §N condition 4 (close it on hardware). Run variants 1-3 strictly serial with kfdsw_probe loaded. The single invariant that closes the condition is map_kva_set == 0 on EVERY display-SW release across all three variants (host CPU-RM has no CPU address to write through), corroborated by (a) unchanged host-side canaries in every region outside the guest's store+guest-RAM, and (b) empty host-dmesg deltas. Variant 1 is the gate's own positive control — it must show dsw_calls>0, or the whole result is 'nothing fired', indistinguishable from today's vacuous pass. Record source revision and kf3 euid/CapEff per run (CLAUDE.md: any bench claim carries the source revision). Mark UNVERIFIED and state so in the result: what GSP firmware does with the 0x9072 methods, which Flags/address it places in SEMAPHORE_SCHEDULE_CALLBACK, and whether hVASpace is the channel's own space.

DEPENDENCY that keeps this a READ-ONLY run — §N condition 'the client split is built' is NOT yet met, and variant 3's canary is its test. §N:397-399 requires the host client the address check uses to hold ONLY the guest's store, guest RAM and twins, with kayfabe's own allocations (broker frame slots) in SEPARATE clients. Today kayfabe opens ONE host client per VM (crates/kf-qemu/src/device.rs HostRm::open, leaked once; V3_DISPLAY 'true security bound' §1), and stage-1 audit S1-21 (identity windows user-reachable in every twin; docs/audits/2026-10-03-v3-stage1.md:446-481) and S1-22 (display compose / libcuda contexts run in that same client; :483-500) show the split is unbuilt. §N:399 itself says this is 'pending the client audit of 2026-10-03'. So the default-on flip cannot proceed until the client split lands AND variant 3 passes against kayfabe's own-allocation canary — which is why the task is correctly scoped to read-only prep.

READY-TO-WRITE (for a LATER write-run, not now) — the §N dated note 'the build needs no host kernel mapping' is already true by construction. nvos46_map_flags clears NVOS46_FLAGS_KERNEL_MAPPING_ENABLE unconditionally after every caller's bits (kf-host/src/lib.rs:258-268), pinned by two tests (lib.rs:2042-2071, 2080+). The kernel-mapping candidate (rev a5d31d5b / 73532bce) was tried on the box (run 4: 5986 rows, 33868 KiB peak host vmap) and changed nothing observable, then dropped; it is not on the branch (traces/.../README.md:86-101; V3_DISPLAY.md review-fixes block (c)). So the note needs only a §N sentence, no code — and it belongs in a write-run after the two conditions above are measured.

CROSS-CHECK against the C oracle's known forging — not a confound here. CLAUDE.md warns the C reference forges completions and is 'no oracle at all for hardware completion'. That caveat is about the Mode-2 C emulator; this entire path is the Rust kf3 twin + REAL host GSP/CPU-RM with a host-side kretprobe witness, and the display-SW release is executed by the real host engine (runs 12-13's Xid 32 prove host execution). The only closed surface is GSP firmware's handling of the 0x9072 methods, which is marked UNVERIFIED throughout and is why the host kretprobe (not any kf3 self-report) is the designated witness.

OPERATIONAL TRAPS to encode in the probe lane (all previously paid for, per CLAUDE.md). (1) kfdsw_probe refuses nothing silently: assert its load line 'kfdsw: loaded N/8 probes' with N=8, and treat a PROBE_REFUSED line as a failed run. (2) Wait for the dispsw_run.sh EXIT line and a non-empty _ktrace.log, never 'the file stopped growing' (a killed detached job leaves a zero-byte file that reads as 'still running'). (3) Persist and assert host dmesg delta is captured (it is the only place a bad-write Xid would show; guest driver dmesg goes to the ssh session, not the serial log). (4) The guest needs ~20-25 s to a login prompt and nvktap0 must pre-exist; a slow boot is not a crash. (5) One QEMU at a time, fresh boot per run.

prep.summary:
VERDICT (client-split lens): the condition is NOT MET as written. It is MET IN SUBSTANCE for the only release writer we can read in source, host CPU-RM. The reason is not a client split: kayfabe never creates a host kernel mapping. Two gaps keep it from being met by construction: mixing a passthrough channel and a Translated ring in one VA space is not refused, and what GSP does with the class's methods is closed (UNVERIFIED).

Revisions read: origin/v3-cand-1 8a682f1b, origin/v3-broker 28b5b6fe (it moved from d36eb75f during the run; the two new commits touch no RM-client code), origin/master 789dee9f, and ogkm-580.159.04 at /workspace/nvidia-gpu-passthrough/research_clones/ogkm-580.159.04. I also used the 10-03 client audit and its verify pass (scratchpad client_audit.json). origin has no v3-p1p2 branch (git ls-remote, 2026-10-04), so S1-21 and S1-23 are still open in candidate 1. Read-only: nothing was edited, committed or pushed, and no box was used. The trees were extracted under the session scratchpad (cand1/, broker/).

Why "not as stated": §N (OWNER_RULINGS.md:400-407 @cand-1) requires the client the check uses to hold only store, guest RAM and twins. On every boot that client (C1, the single HostRm) also holds kayfabe's own VRAM: the 1 MiB Translated ring objects, their channels and CE objects. It also holds completion events, the usermode doorbell object and a ZBC facts object. The guest kernel's CE channels (CeUtils, UVM) are always Translated, so the rings are always there.

Why "in substance": the open-source writer (method_notification.c) writes only through KernelVAddr. That pointer exists only for a map made with NVOS46_FLAGS_KERNEL_MAPPING_ENABLE. kayfabe clears that bit in its single NVOS46 builder, and a source gate pins that. So CPU-RM writes nothing for a display-SW release, whatever the client or VA space. The lookup is also narrower than the docs say. CliGetDmaMappingInfo takes the client and device GSP names and matches exactly one hVASpace, or one VirtualMemory object. It is never client-wide, and hVASpace=0 matches nothing kayfabe owns. A ring can be resolved only from a display-SW channel whose VA space also holds a Translated ring. That is guest-root mixing, which candidate 1 does not refuse, and even then nothing is written.

The client split now only protects against a future kernel mapping. It does not bound the residual closed-GSP path at all; the contents of the VA space do.

Smallest steps that close it:
- (a) The owner restates condition 3 (A.11): no kayfabe map is kernel-mapped, and no VA space holding a display-SW twin's channel holds kayfabe memory.
- (b) A small mixing guard for display-SW spaces, shipped count-only first.
- (c) A per-act census plus a guest-root negative control on the box.
- The literal G/K split is a 3-5 day job (migrate-at-flip). It is needed only if the owner keeps the wording as written.
findings: VERDICT: the condition is NOT MET AS STATED and MET IN SUBSTANCE for host CPU-RM's release writer. That holds through the no-kernel-mapping mask, not through any client separation. Open: guest-root mixing (no refusal) and GSP firmware's handling of NV9072 methods (closed, UNVERIFIED). Revisions: kf-master origin/v3-cand-1 8a682f1b, origin/v3-broker 28b5b6fe, ogkm-580.159.04. origin has no v3-p1p2 (git ls-remote 2026-10-04), so S1-21 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-v3-stage1.md:446) and S1-23 (:518) are unfixed in candidate 1.

C1 = the one guest-facing RM client, one per kf3 device: OwnClient NV01_ROOT_CLIENT (crates/kf-host/src/lib.rs:286-326, minted at :510; opened once at crates/kf-qemu/src/device.rs:290-296). C1 KAYFABE-OWNED objects (this is why the condition fails as written): (1) Translated rings, each a 1 MiB NV01_MEMORY_LOCAL_USER from alloc_device_local (kf-chan/src/host.rs:145-147; the verb's only caller), mapped READ_WRITE at a ring slot inside the guest-kernel mirror (host.rs:148-156; kf-qemu/src/chan.rs:3249-3254; RING_REGION_BASE mem.rs:605). Each ring has a BAR1 CPU view (host.rs:171-191), its own TSG + channel with err_notifier 0 (host.rs:208-216) and a CE object (host.rs:236-238); USERD sits inside the object at +0xF_C000 (host.rs:31). (2) Completion OS events (kf-chan/src/completions.rs:29-48; chan.rs:1203-1230). (3) The usermode doorbell object and its BAR0 view (lib.rs:773-775). (4) A GF100_ZBC_CLEAR facts object (kf-qemu/src/rmfacts.rs:57-71). Kayfabe-PLACED guest memory: the two identity windows (the whole store and all guest RAM) in EVERY mirror (mem.rs:1927-1930, S1-21), and the PRAMIN/BAR1/BAR2 CPU views of the store. Rings exist on every boot, because guest-kernel CE channels are always born Translated (chan.rs:2978-2985), so this is not an edge case.

## 1. The hardware probe for the forced release (condition 4)

The event's `{GPUVA, hVASpace, ReleaseValue, Flags, hClient, hEvent}` are GSP-filled (`g_rpc-structures.h:1672-1681`) — **UNVERIFIED** which VA space / flags / address GSP writes for a given guest method.

The forcing function is the object's `SET_SEMAPHORE` address + value + release-trigger software methods on the passthrough ring. **⚠ A2 (load-bearing): the NVIDIA stack's `0x9072` pushbuffer method encodings are NOT in the open headers** (`cl9072.h` has only the alloc params); nouveau's `0x0400/0x0404/0x0408/0x040c` (`nvkm/engine/sw/gf100.c:62-79`) are a *different driver's* numbers and are not evidence for the NVIDIA GSP path. **Before building the probe, settle the method encoding** by capturing a real NVIDIA guest driver's display-SW pushbuffer on the box (the `nvdiff`/`nvdp` capture style already in-tree), or determine from the capture whether stock clients ever emit an addr+value+release triple at all. The **host kretprobe `kfdsw_probe.ko` is the only ground-truth witness of the cross-VA write** (a guest cannot see it; and because the write is a CPU `MEM_WR32` not a DMA, a **CPU-read canary is also a valid second witness** — A14). Its counters `dsw_calls, map_found, map_null, map_kva_set, map_kva_null, dsw_err` and per-event `va/vas/flags/kernel_mapping` already exist (`scripts/bench/display/kfdsw_probe/kfdsw_probe.c:43-190`), plus the GSP-drain positive control (`drains`, `:192-204`) that distinguishes "none asked" from "probe blind." Assert `kfdsw: loaded 8/8 probes` and treat any `PROBE_REFUSED` line as a failed run. The guest forcing side extends the bench-only shim (`engsw_shim.c`; built in the guest, `.so` never leaves it; wired at `hook.sh` step 4c, `DISPLAY_X11_ENGSW`) to **register a release semaphore at a chosen GPU VA via the object's software methods and arm it** — using the method encodings settled above, not nouveau's. Files to touch (write-run): `scripts/bench/display/engsw_shim/engsw_shim.c` (a release-forcing mode), `scripts/bench/display/hook.sh` (a `DISPLAY_X11_DSW_RELEASE` step), no kf3 code.

**Three variants and pass criteria.** Strictly serial, fresh boot per run (WPR2 resets only on full QEMU restart), `kfdsw_probe` loaded, host-dmesg delta captured and **classified** (A3). The single invariant that closes condition 4 is **`map_kva_set == 0` on every display-SW release** — host CPU-RM has no CPU address to write through, whatever VA it is aimed at.

- **Variant 1 — release aimed at the guest's OWN mapped semaphore page (MANDATORY positive control).** Target: a VA the channel DMA-mapped. Expected: `CliGetDmaMappingInfo` finds it → in bounds → `KernelVAddr` NULL → `KernelVAddr==NULL; semaphore not released` (`LEVEL_ERROR`), `NV_OK`. **Pass: `dsw_calls>0` AND `map_found>0` AND `map_kva_null==dsw_calls` AND `map_kva_set==0`.** Dmesg: a `KernelVAddr==NULL; … not released` line is **expected and benign** (it is the witness the forcing worked — A3); any *other* `NVRM`/`Xid` line fails. Without `dsw_calls>0` this is indistinguishable from today's vacuous pass (the exact trap `kfdsw_probe.c:22-31` was built against).
- **Variant 2 — release aimed INSIDE the store but at a VA this channel's space never mapped.** Expected: no mapping in `(client, hVASpace)` → `NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS`, `Can't find mapping` (`method_notification.c:589`); or a found mapping with `KernelVAddr` NULL. **Pass (corrected per A1): `dsw_calls>0` for this release AND (`map_null>0` or (`map_found>0` & `map_kva_null>0`)) AND `map_kva_set==0` AND a host-side canary pre-written in that store region is byte-unchanged.** The `dsw_calls>0`/`map_*` clause is mandatory so the variant cannot pass vacuously.
- **Variant 3 — release aimed OUTSIDE store AND outside guest RAM (a host-hole VA `[1 TiB−64 GiB, 1 TiB)`, `kf-host/src/channel.rs:95-97`); the variant that directly answers condition 4.** Expected: no mapping → `NV_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS`; and the offset+size bound and the NULL `KernelVAddr` each independently block any write. **Pass: (i) `dsw_calls>0` yet `map_kva_set==0`; (ii) a pre-seeded CPU-read canary over every host region OUTSIDE the guest's store and guest RAM — kayfabe's own host-client allocations (the ring region `RING_REGION_BASE`, the host hole, the identity-window VAs) and, if feasible, a host-RAM page — is byte-unchanged; (iii) dmesg shows only the benign `Can't find mapping`/`KernelVAddr==NULL` lines, no other `NVRM`/`Xid`.** Note: because `map_kva_set==0` blocks ALL writes regardless of target, the canary is a backstop; relying on canary coverage ALONE would be a "pass if it landed somewhere uncovered" hazard, so `map_kva_set==0` is the primary witness. Variant 3's canary is also the client-split check (§2): until the split is built, kayfabe's own allocations share the one client, so this canary tests both at once.

**Overall condition-4 pass:** Variant 1 shows a release fired (`dsw_calls>0`); Variants 1-3 all show `map_kva_set==0`; canaries unchanged; dmesg deltas carry only benign lines. Record source revision and kf3 euid/CapEff per run. State UNVERIFIED in the result: what GSP does with `0x9072` methods, which Flags/address it places in the callback, whether `hVASpace` is the channel's own space (`T-DISPSW-SCOPE`, `V3_SECURITY_MODEL.md:332`), and whether the `LEVEL_ERROR` lines survive the host build's `RmMsg` filter.

### 2. The client-split check (condition 3) and the change needed

Today kayfabe opens **one** guest-facing host client per VM (`OwnClient` `NV01_ROOT_CLIENT`, minted `kf-host/src/lib.rs:296-326`, opened once in realize `device.rs:289-296`). That client holds, besides the guest's store/RAM/twins, **kayfabe's own VRAM**: the 1 MiB Translated rings (`kf-chan/src/host.rs:145-156`), their channels/CE objects, completion events, the usermode doorbell object (full inventory: `client_audit.json` `audit.clients[0].holds`). §N requires the client the address check uses to hold **only** the guest's store, guest RAM and twins; kayfabe's own allocations live in separate clients (`OWNER_RULINGS.md:397-401`).

Two findings that scope this (from source, confirmed by the stage-1 verify pass):
- The §N wording is motivated by a belief the address check is **client-wide**. That is **wrong**: `CliGetDmaMappingInfo` keeps only `VirtualMemory` whose `hVASpace` equals the handle passed, exactly (`mapping_list.c:426-438`, `virtual_mem.c:996`), and every kf `VirtualMemory` carries its own twin space's handle (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:337,396`). So for the writer we can read, the split protects only against a **future** kernel mapping; the writer is bounded by `KernelVAddr`=NULL regardless of client (§4). The `CLIENT-WIDE` claims in `docs/design/V3_DISPLAY.md:315-316,370-371` must be **fold-corrected above the text they correct** (DOC HYGIENE rule 2); `V3_SECURITY_MODEL.md:285-286` flags the need to verify (not a false assertion) and should cite the verify-pass result.
- Where the split still matters: a VA space that holds a display-SW twin's channel **and** a kayfabe ring (the ring breach, `client_audit.json` `guest_steered_paths[2]`: a hostile guest-kernel virtual CE operand/semaphore forwarded unchanged writes the ring, `kf-chan/src/translated.rs:26`), plus the residual closed-GSP path whose reach is the VA space's contents.

Check / change (write-run; count-only first):
- **(a)** A per-act census line `space=<h> rings=<n> kernel_vas=<b>` on every display-SW act (`chan.rs` display-SW act `:2434-2516`; rings from the mirror's `RingSlots`, `mem.rs:612-624`; `kernel_vas` from the mirror `mem.rs:666-667`). Stock Cinnamon/vkcube/glxgears must show `rings=0`.

Do **not** refuse on `kernel_vas`-set — a UVM space legitimately flips to kernel at its first Translated birth (`chan.rs:3214`), and refusing there fails `UVM_REGISTER_GPU` inside `cuInit`. This is the display-SW subset of `T-RING-MIX`, zero cost per op.
- **(c)** Negative control (box): a guest-root kernel module births a kernel CE channel in a dup of the X client's VA space; the census must report `rings=1` (count-only) or a named refusal (enforce). A census that never reported 1 is not trusted (`a_sweep_that_reports_zero_must_first_report_one`). ⚠ The raw client cannot produce this (a kernel_client channel needs internalFlags PRIVILEGE=KERNEL, `chanlink.rs:1366-1378`, verify correction [13]) — it needs a guest kernel module.
- The literal G/K client split (`GuestRm`/`KfRm`, second client, rings migrate-at-flip; `client_audit.json` recommendation item) is **buildable** — dup-into-second-client is settled YES (A9: `sharing.c:345-352`, `standard_mem.c:217`, `os_desc_mem.c:275-282`, and a production store export/import at `device.rs:321,539`) — a 3-5 day structural fix for S1-23. It is needed only if the owner keeps §N's wording verbatim. **Recommend bringing it to the owner as a wording question**: restate condition 3 as the property that bounds the writer — "no kayfabe map is kernel-mapped, and no VA space a display-SW twin's channel runs in holds kayfabe memory (a ring)." The dup settlement means this is a cost/scope decision, not a feasibility unknown.

### 3. The default flip

- **Property default.** `Config::x11_dispsw` (`device.rs:58`) is read through `kf3_realize`'s `x11_dispsw` arg (ABI 13, `ffi_unsafe.rs:104,128`), set from the C `DEFINE_PROP_BOOL("x11-dispsw", …, false)` (`kf3.c:1024`). The flip makes kf3 **enable it by default when the host GPU has a display engine**, without turning it on for display-less hosts. QEMU bool props cannot distinguish unset from false (R4), so use **`OnOffAuto`** (`DEFINE_PROP_ON_OFF_AUTO`): `auto` = on-if-display-engine, matching `display=`'s refuse-if-no-engine shape; explicit `on`/`off` override. Resolve the effective value in `device.rs` realize **after `HostRm::open`** (where `host_classes`/`arch_info` are known). ⊘ **Lower-ABI-risk alternative, noted for the owner:** a plain bool defaulting `true` would degrade to `host_refused` on a host without the engine (graceful, since the guest's own CPU-RM or the host alloc refuses), but it shows the experiment "ON" everywhere and relies on refusal rather than detection — less faithful to §N:402 ("default-on **on hosts whose GPU has a display engine**"). Prefer `OnOffAuto`.
- **"Has a display engine" detection — `NV04_DISPLAY_COMMON (0x0073)` in the host class list.** Use the host's own `NV0080_CTRL_CMD_GPU_GET_CLASSLIST_V2 (0x00800292)`, already read at bring-up (`kf-host/src/lib.rs:663-672`, kept as `host_classes`; decoder `kf-chip/src/host_classes.rs:27`). The authoritative signal is **`0x0073` present**: ogkm strips the display classes on a displayless/fuse-disabled GPU (`gpuRemoveMissingEngineClasses(pGpu, ENG_KERNEL_DISPLAY)`, `gpu.c:2179-2180`, reached when `gpuFuseSupportsDisplay` is false, `kern_disp.c:331-332`, `kern_gpu_ga100.c:45`). - **Refusal by name elsewhere.** On a host with no display-common class, `auto` resolves off and realize prints the reason by name (reuse the shape of `device.rs:634-638`). On a datacenter GPU the flip is unreachable anyway: `display=on` is a precondition (`Config::check`, `device.rs:72-78`) and is itself refused there (A6). The in-VM `host_refused`/`no_twin`/`id_refused` refusals (`dispsw.rs:175-202`) stay as the fallback inside a running VM.
- **Status-line reporting.** Keep the realize line `EXPERIMENT x11-dispsw ON …` (`device.rs:644-647`) and the `dispsw[twins=… host_refused=… no_twin=… capped=… id_refused=… …]` segment (`dispsw.rs:202-220`, empty when off so a default-off line is byte-identical, `the_dispsw_status_segment_is_empty_off_and_counts_on`). Add to the realize line **which signal chose the default** (property explicit vs. auto-from-host-classlist, and the display-common class id seen), and keep `host_refused`/`capped`/`id_refused` visible so a default that does not hold shows (DOC HYGIENE / §M "a bound that does not hold is visible").

### 4. The §N dated note (build needs no host kernel mapping)

True by construction, **no code** — only a §N sentence. `nvos46_map_flags` clears `NVOS46_FLAGS_KERNEL_MAPPING_ENABLE` unconditionally after every caller's bits (`kf-host/src/lib.rs:258-268`), so `KernelVAddr` is NULL for every kayfabe map, and **every `KernelVAddr`-gated writer** — the display-SW semaphore (`method_notification.c:624-635`), the notifier (`:349-359`), **and the sibling timed-semaphore path** `TIMED_SEMAPHORE_RELEASE` → `tsemaRelease` → the same writers (`kernel_gsp.c:1137+`, A12) — writes nothing. The error-notifier ctxdma path is also clear: kayfabe uses no `TYPE_NOTIFIER` and `NVOS03_FLAGS_MAPPING` defaults to `NONE` not `KERNEL` (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:1242-1254`), so its `KernelVAddr` is NULL too (`context_dma.c:543-551`). Therefore the kernel-mapped-bytes cap (condition 2) is **zero by construction**, not a runtime counter — which **reinterprets** condition 2's "cap exists and refuses by name" and must be acknowledged by the owner (A8). Pinned by two tests: `the_kernel_mapping_bit_is_cleared_whatever_the_caller_sets` (`lib.rs:2043-2071`) and `only_the_one_builder_can_name_the_kernel_mapping_bit` (`lib.rs:2080-2139`, a source gate: exactly one `Nvos46Parameters` literal, flags from `nvos46_map_flags`). The kernel-mapping candidate (`a5d31d5b`, run 4: 5986 rows, 33868 KiB peak host vmap, 0 refused) changed nothing observable and is **not on the branch** (`6082f264`). **Proposed §N sentence:** *"The build needs no host kernel mapping for display-SW (or timed-semaphore) releases; `nvos46_map_flags` clears `KERNEL_MAPPING` on every map, so `KernelVAddr` is NULL and host RM writes no memory on any `KernelVAddr`-gated release — the kernel-mapped-bytes cap is therefore zero by construction, pinned by the map-flag builder test.
